You are writing the current research update for AI Macro.

Use only the findings and recent developments in the supplied briefing. Decide what matters, connect related evidence when the relationship is supported, and explain it in clear, natural English for an intelligent general reader. Prioritize significance over coverage. It is fine for the evidence to be mixed. Do not force unrelated facts into one story.

The style reference shows the desired level of restraint, specificity, and sentence construction. Match those qualities without copying its wording. Write like a careful human analyst. Use concrete subjects and verbs. Avoid rhetorical gimmicks and artificial-sounding transitions. Do not mention the prompt, the briefing, evidence IDs, validation, methodology, or the writing process.

On a normal update, candidate_domains identifies sections that may deserve replacement. Update only the domain Reads for which you can write something materially more useful than the prior publication; you may return no domain Reads when none deserves replacement. On a bootstrap publication, write every candidate domain because no prior Read exists. Always write one new Macro Read that explains the most important current story across the platform in two to four coherent paragraphs.

Do not inventory every supplied metric or news item. Use a number only when it helps the reader understand magnitude. Use recent developments when they materially sharpen the interpretation of the measured findings. Treat news reports as reported developments, not as proof of a broader causal claim.

Attach only the fact_ids and event_ids that actually support each passage. Those IDs are citations for the application and must never appear in the prose. Do not invent numbers, facts, events, causes, or forecasts.

Return only the structured response.

data_center.analysis: Available records list 3,068 operating sites and 1,556 sites in development, equivalent to roughly one development site for every two operating sites. Separately, 894 sites are tracked in the active pipeline. Recent reports identify two concrete execution risks: a Texas moratorium on data-center approvals was broadened to include environmental permits, while Oracle issued a force majeure notice following setbacks at Project Jupiter. These cases do not establish a failure rate for the wider pipeline, but they show why site counts should not be read as completed capacity.

economic_impact.analysis: Nonfarm-business productivity grew 2.2% as real output rose 2.5%. Real hourly compensation increased 0.6%, while unit labor costs grew 1.4%, indicating positive aggregate performance without a comparable increase in real compensation. A report that investors are pricing in a 32.6% AI productivity boost for software engineers describes an expectation for a specific workforce segment, not an economy-wide result. The current aggregate data do not identify AI's contribution.

Utility Dive reported that FERC rejected most of PJM’s large-load interconnection plan, days after PJM approved fast-track interconnection for 2.1 GW from Engie and LS Power. Individual projects can advance even while rules for larger-load connections remain unsettled; the decisions do not alter the low historical conversion rate.

macro.analysis: Public equity and credit markets are applying a sharper test to AI exposure. The AI Equity Index fell materially to 30.2 and the median one-year return to 11.4%, even as Reuters reported that AI-related companies were expected to drive most third-quarter U.S. earnings gains. Reuters also reported record-high default insurance for U.S. technology credits amid AI concerns, and the Financial Times reported selling in data-center bonds. The Chicago Fed NFCI remains at -0.50 after a 0.02 increase over three months, so the reports point to stress in exposed assets rather than demonstrating broad financial tightening. Broad hardware production is expanding alongside a large data-center pipeline, although the production series are not AI-specific. Computer and peripheral-equipment output is growing 9.2%, semiconductor and electronic-component output 11.5%, and available records list 1,556 data-center sites in development—roughly one for every two operating sites. Delivery is less certain: only 24.2% of the 2,061 GW active interconnection queue is at executed-agreement or construction stages, and only 13% of the 2000–2020 queue cohort reached operation. Utility Dive’s reports that FERC rejected most of PJM’s large-load interconnection plan while PJM approved fast-track interconnection for 2.1 GW of named projects illustrate selective progress, not broad resolution of the queue. Downstream diffusion remains less decisive. Businesses expecting AI use within six months edged up to 27.7%, but this is 3.9 percentage points above current use. Only one tracked AI-linked labor channel has positive employment growth, with power and communication construction leading at 0.8%. Nonfarm-business productivity is growing 2.2%, while real hourly compensation is growing 0.6%; these aggregate measures do not identify AI’s contribution. The data therefore show positive productivity and a modest rise in adoption expectations, but not broad labor-market diffusion or a demonstrated economy-wide AI effect.
